name: skills
tagline: A tool for finding and installing ready-made skills into AI coding agents - one command, and it works across 75+ agents.
sentence: Install a new ability into your AI coding agent with one command - for example, a design-taste skill that makes every interface your agent builds look polished instead of generic.

board.say: You want your AI coding agent to follow specific practices - design standards, testing rules, coding conventions - but writing those instructions yourself takes time, and they don't transfer between agents.
board.eg: You wrote a page of design guidelines for Claude Code, but now you want the same rules in Cursor and Codex - and each agent stores instructions in a different folder.

board.say: You run a command in your terminal and pick a skill from the directory at skills.sh.
board.eg: Type `npx skills add vercel-labs/agent-skills` and Vercel's official skill pack installs into every agent on your machine.

board.say: A skill name or search term - a GitHub project like `vercel-labs/agent-skills`, or a keyword like 'react testing'.
board.eg: `npx skills find typescript` searches the directory and shows matching skills with their install counts.

board.say: It finds the skill, downloads it, and installs it into the right folder for each of your AI coding agents.
steps: Finds the skill in the skills.sh directory (over 600K skills listed) or directly from GitHub, GitLab, or a URL
Downloads it and places it in the correct folder for your agents - Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, or any of 75+ others
Your agent loads the skill automatically when a matching task comes up - full instructions load on demand, not all at once
board.eg: The README's example: install a 'react testing' skill and the next time you ask your agent to write tests for a React component, it follows the skill's testing practices automatically.

board.say: Your AI coding agents have new, shared abilities - installed once, available across every supported agent on your machine.

outputs.eg: One install command puts a design skill into Claude Code, Cursor and Codex at the same time
skills.sh lists over 600K skills with install counts, categories and security scans from Snyk
`npx skills init` creates a template - write instructions once and share them with your team or publish them to the directory

before: Adding a new ability to your AI coding agent means writing instructions from scratch, and those instructions only work in one agent - switching agents means rewriting them.
There is no central place to find, compare or share ready-made agent instructions. You copy snippets from blog posts and hope they work.
after: One command installs a skill into every agent on your machine - Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and 75+ others, all at once.
A searchable directory at skills.sh lists hundreds of thousands of skills, ranked by installs, with categories and security scans.
uses_note: Skills.sh reports over 3.9M installs for its top skill (find-skills). Individual named adopters are hard to find because skills install silently into agents and leave no public trace.

pulse.history_note: Created Jan 14, 2026. Launched Jan 20 with the skills.sh directory. The format started at Anthropic and was released as an open standard in December 2025.

steps: Search for a skill: run `npx skills find react` (or any topic you care about) in your terminal and browse the results.
Install one: run `npx skills add vercel-labs/agent-skills` to install [Vercel's official skill pack](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-skills) into your agents.
Check it worked: run `npx skills list` to see which skills are installed and which agents they landed in.
try.paste:
/skillspector https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills

If that scan passes: run `npx skills find react`, pick a skill from the results, install it with `npx skills add`, then run `npx skills list` to confirm. 10 minutes max.

footprint.disk: No permanent install needed. Runs via `npx` (requires Node.js). Skills themselves are small text files - a SKILL.md plus optional scripts and references.
footprint.memory: No data found. The tool runs briefly to install or search, then exits. Skills are loaded by the agent, not by the tool.
footprint.runs_on: Mac, Windows and Linux. Requires Node.js (for npx). The tool installs skills for whichever agents are already on your machine.

best_for: You use an AI coding agent and want to add abilities - design taste, testing rules, coding standards - without writing instructions from scratch
You work across multiple agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex) and want the same skills in all of them with one install command
skip_if: You already have a well-tuned set of agent instructions and don't want a tool overwriting or conflicting with them
You are concerned about running unreviewed third-party instructions in your coding agent - the directory has no human review gate

alternatives.name: Agent Skills specification
alternatives.line: The open standard behind skills. You can write and install SKILL.md files by hand without the skills tool or the skills.sh directory.

alternatives.name: Agent-specific instructions
alternatives.line: Write instructions directly for one agent: CLAUDE.md for Claude Code, .cursorrules for Cursor. More control, but no cross-agent sharing.

watch: **No human review gate.** Skills.sh lists over 600K skills with no submission or curation process. Rankings come from install counts alone, which one independent reviewer notes 'can be gamed.'

**Security researchers bypassed the malicious-skill detector.** Trail of Bits got data-exfiltrating skills marked safe. Vercel's response is a real-time scanning partnership with Snyk rather than human review.
**Skills run inside your agent with your permissions.** A skill's instructions become part of what your agent does. Review what you install, especially from unknown publishers.

**The ecosystem is 9 months old.** The format started at Anthropic and was released as an open standard in December 2025. Adoption is broad (75+ agents, 20+ platforms) but the trust model is still maturing.
